name: Microsoft
summary: Recruiter-guided interviews that vary by team, often virtual, with coding for engineering roles and a strong focus on growth mindset.

process.note: Microsoft says the steps vary by role and your recruiter explains the format. The round mix below is commonly reported for software roles, not official.

stages.name: Recruiter conversation
stages.detail: Your recruiter explains the format and timeline for your role.

stages.name: Screen
stages.detail: Candidates often report a technical screen with an engineer before the main interviews.

stages.name: Interviews
stages.detail: You may meet future teammates and cross-functional colleagues. Some roles include coding exercises. Many interviews are virtual.

stages.name: Decision
stages.detail: Feedback is typically combined, sometimes with a final conversation with the hiring manager.

design.note: Design rounds are commonly reported for experienced roles, often around collaboration, sync and cloud services.

values.title: Culture and values
values.summary: Microsoft's interview tips name the parts of its culture it looks for, built on a growth mindset. The names are Microsoft's; the explanations are ours.

items.name: Growth mindset
items.gist: Be a learner: pick up new skills fast and build on others' ideas.

items.name: Diverse and inclusive
items.gist: Notice your own blind spots and seek out different views.

items.name: One Microsoft
items.gist: Work across team lines and build on other people's success.

items.name: Customer obsession
items.gist: Understand customers' experiences and let that shape your work.

items.name: Respect, integrity, accountability
items.gist: Treat people well, act honestly and own your results.

prompts.text: Describe a time you had to learn something unfamiliar quickly to unblock your team.
Tell a story about working with another team whose goals differed from yours.
Talk about feedback that changed how you work. What did you do differently?
Share a mistake you owned publicly and how you made it right.
